{
  "reframes": [
    {
      "bottleneck": "The error floor lives in the fixed LOPLS-AA parameters, not in sampling. Once Green-Kubo noise is below the force-field bias (already true at 6x5 ns replicas), every added molecule or replica re-measures the same chemistry-dependent bias; time-parallel or longer sampling only shrinks noise that is not binding. Compute buys more of the same.",
      "assumption": "The force field must be taken as given: the ~25% floor is a fact to be documented, not a bias that compute can repair.",
      "reframe": "Change the unit of work from 'molecule at fixed force field' to 'force-field variant per molecule': derive per-molecule atomic charges from a cheap DFT single point (RESP-style) and rerun short Green-Kubo. If error drops, additional compute (more refit molecules, then class-specific LJ refits or delta-ML corrections) lowers the floor itself instead of documenting it.",
      "question": "On 12 molecules spanning C10-C50 and both hydrocarbon and ester chemistries, do per-molecule DFT/RESP charges cut held-out viscosity mean absolute percent error below 15% where stock LOPLS-AA charges give ~25%?",
      "measure": "Pick 12 molecules from the published set's high- and low-error ends (6 hydrocarbons, 6 esters). DFT single point plus RESP fit per molecule (~1 CPU-hour each, a few dollars), then 2x3 ns Green-Kubo per molecule at 40 C on one GPU, scoring viscosity error vs stock charges at identical sampling. Roughly $25-35 and a few days wall time.",
      "compute_after": "If the refit clears 15%, spend the full ~$950 on 120 charge refits plus an LJ correction fit, where each added dollar reduces error; if it partially works, escalate to class-specific LJ refits before any raw 120-molecule run.",
      "exact": "Per-molecule |eta_sim - eta_meas|/eta_meas at 40 C, averaged over the 12, stock vs refit charges at identical sampling; success = refit MAPE <= 15% and at least 10 percentage points below stock MAPE.",
      "expected": "Esters improve most, since their polarity is where generic charges err; MAPE falls from ~25% to ~12-18% and the viscosity bias sign shrinks or flips in at least 8 of 12 molecules.",
      "fails_if": "Refit MAPE stays >= 20% or improves by < 5 points: the floor then sits in LJ/dispersion or the transport model, not in charges, and per-molecule refits are not the lever.",
      "closest_prior": "Ogbomo 2026 ran stock LOPLS-AA only [s_ogbomo_md]; RESP charge derivation (Bayly 1993) is standard in OPLS/GAFF parameterization but was never varied in this benchmark [s_ogbomo_res]."
    },
    {
      "bottleneck": "The plan spends ~$940 mapping a floor it already hypothesizes, and defers the only test that could change the answer - whether a bias correction generalizes - to the largest, last set size. Steps are ordered biggest-spend-first.",
      "assumption": "A bias correction can only be fitted and validated once 120 molecules are in hand; the published 8 cannot support a correction model.",
      "reframe": "Invert the order of steps: fit a small chemistry-conditioned correction (chain length x ester/hydrocarbon, 2-4 parameters) on the already-published 8 molecules at zero MD cost, then buy the cheapest discriminating held-out set - 16 molecules at the corners of the correction axes - and scale only if the frozen correction generalizes. Additional molecules now buy correction generality, a different answer, rather than a finer map of the same floor.",
      "question": "Does a correction of at most 4 parameters fitted only on Ogbomo's 8 molecules hold on 16 held-out molecules, with held-out viscosity MAPE <= 15% and Spearman rank correlation >= 0.9 against measurement?",
      "measure": "Select 16 molecules at the extremes of chain length and chemistry from the 835-molecule set, run the existing protocol (6x5 ns, ~$4-5 per molecule at plan throughput, roughly $60-75 total), fit the correction on the published 8, freeze it, and score the 16. About one week.",
      "compute_after": "If it generalizes, the remaining 104 molecules (~$800) each tighten the correction and extend its domain, so compute changes predictions; if it fails, stop at ~$60 instead of $940.",
      "exact": "Held-out MAPE and Spearman rho on the 16 molecules using a correction fitted on 8 and frozen before scoring; success = MAPE <= 15% and rho >= 0.9; indeterminate band 15-20%.",
      "expected": "If the floor is a smooth function of chemistry as the hypothesis claims, held-out MAPE lands near 12-18% and rho near 0.8-0.95; thermal conductivity needs only a uniform down-shift since it is over-predicted for all 8 calibration molecules.",
      "fails_if": "Held-out MAPE >= 25% or rho <= 0.7 for every smooth correction family: the bias is not chemistry-smooth, no correction will generalize, and the 120-molecule run would only confirm the floor.",
      "closest_prior": "The bias signs and floor hypothesis come from the same 8-molecule study [s_ogbomo_res]; the closest prior calibration size is 8 [s_ogbomo_md] - this tests whether 8 was already enough."
    },
    {
      "bottleneck": "What is measured - absolute viscosity and thermal conductivity at a single 40 C state point - is exactly where the force field is worst. Rank information is swamped by a chemistry-dependent offset that no amount of single-temperature sampling removes, so extra compute at 40 C cannot change the ranking.",
      "assumption": "The quantity that must rank correctly is the absolute 40 C transport value.",
      "reframe": "Change what is measured: rank candidates by their simulated temperature response (slope of log viscosity vs 1/T over 25-60 C, i.e., viscous activation energy, and the conductivity temperature ratio), where a multiplicative force-field error largely cancels. Compute spent at extra temperatures buys new discriminating signal instead of re-measuring a biased constant.",
      "question": "On the 8 published molecules, does the Spearman rank correlation between simulated and measured viscosity temperature-slope (d log eta / d(1/T) over 25-60 C) exceed 0.9, where absolute 40 C values sit below 0.7?",
      "measure": "Reuse the published protocol at 25 and 60 C on the same 8 molecules: 8 molecules x 2 temperatures x 6 replicas x 5 ns = 96 replicas, roughly $75 at plan throughput (halve replicas for ~$40). Regress log eta vs 1/T per molecule, compute Spearman rho of simulated vs measured slopes, and compare to the rho of 40 C absolutes.",
      "compute_after": "If slope ranking holds, the campaign becomes 3 temperatures x 40-120 molecules; every added molecule-temperature buys rank-relevant signal (roughly $2,800 for the full 120, or the same $950 over 40 molecules).",
      "exact": "Spearman rho between simulated and measured d(log eta)/d(1/T) across the 8 molecules, versus rho between simulated and measured eta at 40 C; success = slope-rho >= 0.9 and at least 0.2 above absolute-rho.",
      "expected": "If the dominant force-field error is a prefactor (consistent with a uniform over-prediction sign), simulated slopes rank 7-8 of 8 molecules correctly and slope-rho reaches 0.9+.",
      "fails_if": "Simulated slopes show rho <= 0.7 against measurement, or simulated activation energies are near-constant across molecules so there is no discriminating signal: the error is not a simple prefactor and the reframe is dead.",
      "closest_prior": "Ogbomo 2026 scored only single-temperature (40 C) absolutes on these molecules [s_ogbomo_md]; the reference set holds measured multi-temperature data that has not been used for scoring [s_ogbomo_db]."
    }
  ]
}
